strengths: Well-motivated and clearly articulated problem. The observation that fusing per-frame geometry into a single global point cloud accumulates cross-view misalignment (Fig. 1, Fig. 2) is convincing and is directly backed by the controlled rendering diagnostic in Appendix H.1 (44.93 dB for a single local point cloud vs. 16.15 dB after fusing ~45 frames).

The system design is non-trivial and internally coherent: per-frame local point-cloud memory, a coverage-driven retrieval formulated as visibility-coverage maximization (Section 3.3, Fig. 2, Algorithm 1), a multi-anchor weaving controller with shared cross-anchor attention, pose-conditioned importance-weighted fusion, and complementary target-pose control (Section 3.4, Fig. 3). Each of these pieces is subsequently ablated rather than merely asserted.

The empirical study is broad by the standards of this venue: two DiT backbones (CogVideoX-I2V-5B, Wan2.2-TI2V-5B), two datasets (RealEstate10K, DL3DV), eight baselines, and ablations on global vs. local memory (Table 2), fusion strategy (Fig. 5a), joint vs. separate attention (Fig. 5b), retrieval budget K (Table 3), efficiency (Table 4), history-length scaling (Fig. 8), plus a 2400-frame explore-and-revisit stress test (Fig. 10).

The long-horizon stress test is a genuinely informative piece of evidence: Fig. 10 shows SPMem's global point cloud becoming impractical around frame 1120 while AnchorWeave retains ~20 dB revisit PSNR over the first ~1000 frames, directly instantiating the paper's central hypothesis.

Reporting quality is generally good: failure modes (view-dependent reflective surfaces, Fig. 13; pose drift and accumulated synthesis error), cost trade-offs (Table 4: 221 s/34 GB vs. 275 s/39 GB at K=4), and an explicit Limitations section are provided rather than hidden.
weaknesses: The individual ingredients are largely pre-existing: anchor-video conditioning (Gen3C, TrajCrafter, ViewCrafter, EPiC), retrieval-based memory (Context-as-Memory), ControlNet-style control branches, and attention-based fusion of multiple conditions. The delta is essentially 'use per-frame local point clouds instead of a fused global one, and fuse K anchors with pose-weighted attention,' which is an incremental recombination rather than a new formulation or training paradigm.

The headline comparison in Table 1 is confounded by backbone. AnchorWeave's best numbers (total 80.98, PSNR 24.04, SSIM 0.6739) come from Wan2.2-5B, while no baseline is evaluated on Wan2.2. On the shared CogVideoX backbone the margin over SEVA is marginal or negative (total 80.80 vs. 79.66, but PSNR 20.96 vs. 21.13 and only +0.0016 SSIM). The claim of 'significantly' better quality is therefore not supported by a matched-backbone, matched-budget comparison.

Baseline treatment is not fully fair. Context-as-Memory and SPMem are reimplemented on a different backbone (CogVideoX) with LoRA rank 16 / 10K steps, and ViewCrafter/Gen3C/TrajCrafter/EPiC are further driven by the authors' own retrieval strategy ('K-1' anchors). A ~4 dB PSNR gap over a reimplemented SPMem could plausibly reflect reimplementation/tuning quality rather than a methodological advantage, and no evidence (e.g., reproducing published numbers for the reimplemented methods) is given to rule this out.

The central ablation (Table 2) is confounded with the number of conditioning anchors: the 'global' setting renders one anchor from the fused global memory, whereas the 'local' setting uses up to K=4 local anchors, so the 16.31 -> 20.96 dB gap mixes the memory representation with the multi-anchor conditioning. The paper's own Table 3 (K=1 local: 19.01 dB) allows partial disentangling, but a matched-budget global-memory control (global memory with K anchors, same controller) is never run, so the core claim 'local geometry beats global fusion' is not cleanly isolated.

The two closest 3D-memory methods discussed in Related Work, Spatia [119] and MagicWorld [49], are cited as the most similar 'global 3D point cloud as memory' approaches yet are never evaluated against, qualitatively or quantitatively. This is a conspicuous omission given that they are the natural points of comparison for the paper's central argument.

Evaluation is dominated by PSNR/SSIM against GT frames in a partial-revisit protocol (49 target / 21 history frames from the same clip). Because target views overlap retrieved history, these metrics reward faithful copying of anchor renderings more than generative fidelity in newly-exposed regions, and they are known to correlate poorly with perceived video quality. No perceptual/user study supports the repeated 'significantly improves visual quality' claims, and no FVD or equivalent distributional metric is reported.

Long-horizon and open-domain claims rest entirely on hand-picked qualitative frames (Figs. 7, 16-19). The generalization statement (Section 4.5) asserts consistency 'at frame 1 and in later frames... in the final frame (frame 222)' and '360-degree panoramic consistency' without any quantitative long-horizon metric in the general free-form setting; the only quantitative long-horizon result is the synthetic explore-and-revisit stress test of Appendix H.2.

Several design choices appear ad hoc or are inconsistently described, which hurts reproducibility. For example, the controller is stated to be applied 'during the first 90% of denoising steps' in Section 4.1 but 'during the first 80% of denoising steps' in Appendix A.1; anchor injection is restricted to the 'first third' of backbone layers without justification or sensitivity analysis; and empty retrieval slots are padded with 'fully-invisible anchor clips,' whose effect on the attention/fusion path is not analyzed.

Cost is not negligible and is quietly growing with the design: multi-anchor control adds ~25% wall-clock time and 5 GB GPU memory at K=4 (Table 4), before counting per-frame TTT3R geometry estimation, retrieval, and anchor rendering. The method also inherits the failure modes of the external 3D estimator (the paper acknowledges out-of-distribution scenes degrade anchors), so the robustness claim is bounded by a component the paper does not analyze or improve.
